decision: Use a two-stage real-Qubes qualification gate: read-only qrexec policy/service smoke first, then synthetic fenced mutation/recovery campaign.
scope: Defensive synthetic qualification only. No real financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflows, or weakened security controls.

context.transportQualification: Execution-derived process-boundary qualification already exists for before-mutation, post-claim, post-heartbeat, post-fail, post-complete, and post-journal-commit crash points.
context.remainingGap: The same invariants have not yet been proven across an actual worker-Qube -> qrexec policy/service -> coordinator-Qube boundary.
context.ciConstraint: GitHub-hosted jobs on the current head have failed before step 1 with runner_id=0, so workflow failure is not code-test evidence.

correctness.preferred: read-only smoke then synthetic mutation campaign
correctness.reason: Separates policy/service/identity/framing defects from MissionQueue mutation semantics before testing state changes.

robustnessSecurity.preferred: read-only smoke then synthetic mutation campaign
robustnessSecurity.reason: Keeps first real-VM interaction non-mutating, preserves HMAC/Ed25519/fencing checks, and fails closed before any synthetic claim if transport identity or policy is wrong.

latencyResourcesRegression.preferred: read-only smoke then synthetic mutation campaign
latencyResourcesRegression.reason: Adds no daemon, database, WAL, or production round trip beyond the qrexec calls being qualified; avoids expanding Slice 1/2 semantics while executable QA is blocked.

approaches.name: Direct mutable real-Qubes campaign
approaches.qa: Poor fault isolation: policy/auth/framing failures can mask mutation-state defects.

approaches.name: Read-only policy/service smoke followed by synthetic fenced mutation campaign
approaches.qa: Strong fault isolation and explicit phase gates.

approaches.name: More local process emulation before Qubes
approaches.qa: Diminishing returns because process-boundary crash qualification already exists and cannot validate real qrexec policy/service installation.

requirements: worker Qube reaches only the intended qrexec service in the coordinator Qube
request authentication and response Ed25519 attestation verify against the expected deployment identity
one request produces one bounded response with no secret/token reflection
policy denial, malformed framing, stale deployment identity, and authentication failure all fail closed
claim -> heartbeat -> complete succeeds across separate qrexec process calls using the same live fenced lease
claim/heartbeat/fail unknown post-mutation crashes remain request-bound attested indeterminate and do not remutate
complete unknown post-mutation crash reconciles read-only only when exact durable postcondition is proven
all evidence is synthetic and bound to exact Git SHA/runtime/service/key identity

readinessRule: Do not classify REAL-WORKER READY until Mission Runtime QA and Qubes Transport QA execute green on the exact candidate SHA and both real-Qubes phases pass. LAB READY remains the maximum classification beforehand.
failuresLessons: A red workflow with runner_id=0 and steps=[] is infrastructure non-execution, not a code-test failure or pass.
Process-boundary qualification is necessary but cannot prove qrexec policy/service installation or VM identity boundaries.
Do not add new mission reliability semantics merely to compensate for absent executable CI evidence.
Transport/authentication faults should be isolated with a non-mutating probe before state-changing synthetic tests.
nextTask: Implement the phase-1 read-only qrexec policy/service acceptance contract and test harness on the current Slice 2 branch, without enabling a real worker or any real side effect.
